THE_A_GATE_WAS_PASSED_WITH_ROOM_TO_SPARE.fact: The harm is NEGATIVE with its entire interval below zero: 5A_1D beat balanced 3A_3D on Pole A by +0.125 [+0.042, +0.208]. The gate asked only that harm not exceed 0.10.
THE_A_GATE_WAS_PASSED_WITH_ROOM_TO_SPARE.the_planning_arithmetic_was_about_this_c: The sizing before the freeze showed that at about 40% discordance the gate at n=128 needed the true harm to be at most -0.008, and that a composition exactly equal to the baseline passed only 42% of the time (60% at n=192). The observed discordance was 34%, and the true effect turned out to be a genuine advantage, the -0.08 to -0.12 rows of that table. The refined A-failure interpretation was never exercised.
THE_A_GATE_WAS_PASSED_WITH_ROOM_TO_SPARE.consistency_across_halves: Both seed halves agree in sign and size (-0.135, -0.115), unlike the exploratory sweep, whose Pole-A contrasts flipped sign between halves.

CORRECTION_TO_THE_EXPLORATORY_SWEEP_READ.what_the_sweep_reading_said: Pole A is a plateau across 3 to 6 attackers with no distinguishable best composition; an attack-heavy composition costs A nothing.
CORRECTION_TO_THE_EXPLORATORY_SWEEP_READ.what_the_fresh_data_says: 5A_1D is BETTER than 3A_3D on Pole A, with an interval excluding zero. The sweep saw the same sign and a similar size (+0.078 [-0.078, +0.234]) but at n=64 could not exclude zero.
CORRECTION_TO_THE_EXPLORATORY_SWEEP_READ.the_revised_safest_wording: On Pole A, 5A/1D outperformed the balanced 3A/3D baseline on fresh seeds. Whether Pole A distinguishes among the attack-heavy compositions (4A_2D, 5A_1D, 6A_0D) was NOT tested here; only 5A_1D and 3A_3D were run.
CORRECTION_TO_THE_EXPLORATORY_SWEEP_READ.not_a_reversal: The sweep's statement was about what n=64 could distinguish. It was accurate as a description of that data and is superseded on the 5A_1D versus 3A_3D contrast only.

COMPARISON_TO_THE_EXPLORATORY_SWEEP_NOT_.reading: The Pole-B effect replicated at essentially the same size. The Pole-B 5A_1D win rate came in 0.057 lower than the sweep's, the modest shrinkage expected when a composition was chosen partly for looking good on that block. The fresh estimate is the unbiased one.

CLAIM_ADOPTED_FROM_THE_FREEZE.sentence: For the tested 6v6 regimes, a fixed attack-heavy composition is sufficient to recover the B-side behavioral advantage while preserving strong A-side performance.
CLAIM_ADOPTED_FROM_THE_FREEZE.what_it_is_relative_to: The balanced 3A/3D baseline. Only two arms ran.
CLAIM_ADOPTED_FROM_THE_FREEZE.scripted_not_learned: This is a scripted 6v6 composition confirmation, not a learned-specialization experiment. A pass tells us that the selected fixed composition works across the two 6v6 poles. It does not tell us that the old learned pi_B problem has been solved.
CLAIM_ADOPTED_FROM_THE_FREEZE.the_hypothesis_still_open: That learned policies already play attack-heavy on B, leaving a B specialist nothing to specialize toward, remains a hypothesis linking two different objects. Nothing here tests it.

WHAT_IS_NOT_ESTABLISHED: That routing could not add value beyond 5A_1D. Per-pole compositions (4A_2D on A, 6A_0D on B) were not run. The exploratory sweep put the Pole-B headroom of 6A_0D over 5A_1D at +0.078 [-0.031, +0.203] at n=64, which is not excluded.
That 6v6 is solved generally, or that any result carries to opponents other than these two certified poles.
That team size caused any difference from 4v4.
Anything about learned specialization, PPO, or learned coordination.

CROSS_SCALE_OBSERVATION_DESCRIPTIVE_NOT_.frozen_clause: The 6v6 composition runs use the certified 6v6 pole pair. Pole B is canonical SDS_PARENT_OP7, not the 4v4 B3-3 SDS2_B3_LOCKDEF10_2V1 construction. Therefore cross-scale differences cannot be attributed solely to team size.
CROSS_SCALE_OBSERVATION_DESCRIPTIVE_NOT_.observation: At 4v4 the balanced and attack-heavy compositions pulled the two poles in opposite directions (all-attack hurt Pole A), which is why a guarded router was needed. At 6v6 a single attack-heavy composition beat the balanced baseline on BOTH poles.
CROSS_SCALE_OBSERVATION_DESCRIPTIVE_NOT_.why_only_descriptive: The two scales differ in more than team size: Pole B's construction (B3-3 versus canonical OP7), the size-normalized defender gate (min_alive_for_defender 4 versus 6), and the compositions available. The comparison is also baseline-relative in each case (2A/2D at 4v4, 3A/3D at 6v6).

OPEN_DECISIONS_FOR_THE_PI_NONE_STARTED.note: The frozen spec authorizes this confirmation only.
OPEN_DECISIONS_FOR_THE_PI_NONE_STARTED.candidate_1_read_only_probe_of_existing_: Measure the role composition the existing learned 6v6 specialists actually play, by tick, on both poles. That tests the open hypothesis directly, with no training, using checkpoints that already exist. It connects the scripted finding to the learned failure.
OPEN_DECISIONS_FOR_THE_PI_NONE_STARTED.candidate_2_use_5A_1D_as_a_scripted_targ: The frozen main-line sequence ends at learned coordination. This result supplies a scripted 6v6 reference and the guarded-router result supplies a 4v4 one. PPO has been off throughout and this record does not authorize it.
OPEN_DECISIONS_FOR_THE_PI_NONE_STARTED.candidate_3_routing_headroom_at_6v6: Only if routing headroom is the question: a fresh-seed comparison of 5A_1D against the per-pole exploratory argmaxes. The sweep suggests small headroom.

claim_boundary: Two certified 6v6 poles, fixed scripted composition, PPO off, n=192 paired seeds, SEALED. Does not authorize a router, PPO, learned coordination, or any statement about other opponents.
